column1: # harness/gates.tsv — the factory gate registry (Gate I, control-structure plan slice 6).
# Every factory gate is registered here with the END-TO-END denial probe(s) that demonstrate
# it blocks the prohibited action (the run does not advance / the receipt is rejected / the
# status is not written), and the RED-NOW mutation that would turn the probe red (falsifiability
# — a probe that cannot be turned red is theater). `scripts/check_denial_probes.py` reads this
# file at build time and fails the build if any gate has no probe, any probe node-id does not
# collect in the suite, or any gate's red_now is empty. `harness/denial_probe.sh` re-runs a
# gate's probes on demand. A gate without a registered, collecting, passing probe is theater.
# Columns are TAB-separated: gate | name | prohibits | probes | red_now
#   gate      — the gate id (A–N + the named residuals F3/F4/R2/R3)
#   name      — the gate's short label (the gate name + the failure shape it closes)
#   prohibits — the prohibited action, stated end-to-end (what does NOT happen when the gate fires)
#   probes    — semicolon-separated pytest node-ids (file::test_name) that assert the block
#   red_now   — the specific mutation of the gate that turns its probe red (falsifiability)
# This file is data, not code: the generic harness reads it; a target never edits it. Adding a
# new factory gate without a row here fails `make ship` — which is the point.

column5: check_denial_probes.py accepts a gates.tsv with a gate whose probes column is empty, or a probe node-id that does not collect

column5: dispatch_lane.sh launches a lane with no authority tuple, or with interpretation_confirmed unset

column5: promotion_gate.py grounds a decision on a receipt id not in the chain / a self-consistent forged envelope / a tampered (hash does not re-derive) chain entry

column5: promotion_gate.py grounds a decision on a chain carrying two entries for one receipt id

column5: promotion.py promotes a Standard surface with deterministic=False + no flake receipt (the false close on a load-bearing flake_count)
